dedupe_keys.name: foundation rail infrastructure australia railway lines sidings and stations

description: Foundation Rail Infrastructure is Australia's national rail feature dataset in the Foundation Spatial Data Framework transport theme. It combines the locations and attributes of rail line features (railways, rail sidings, and tramlines including light rail) and rail points (stations, recognised stopping places where passengers board or freight is loaded, whether or not in use) from publicly available data across all states and territories. Sources are the state data custodians (for example NSW Spatial Services, Queensland and Victoria's departments and Land Tasmania), with Geoscience Australia data used for Western Australia, the Northern Territory and South Australian points because of licensing restrictions. Coverage is national; the railway lines layer has 29,706 features. It is free under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence with open access, served as ArcGIS feature services in the Digital Atlas of Australia and as a Geoscience Australia map service. Caveats: attributes and currency vary with the source jurisdiction, and some stations may be disused. The network supports rail network flow and capacity models, criticality analysis and hazard exposure of Australian railways. It complements the Australian national roads dataset.
